title: Decide how the papyrus CLI signs in without Prospectus
description: Agents and editors use the signed-in `papyrus` CLI. On the existing sites remote login goes through Prospectus, which Humorus does not use at launch. Decide and document the sign-in path for this deployment (the newsroom's own Google sign-in, or IAM through the single sign-on profile for operators), and file the Papyrus issue if neither works.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
**Recommendation: local loopback login for editors, and `papyrus login --remote` for agents and headless machines. No Prospectus needed.**

Source: Papyrus docs/cli-login.md, amplify/cli-login/remote-login.ts, amplify/site-backend.ts (read-only research; design in PPY-5a3624). PPY-1a6aa6 could not be read from the Papyrus board, so its status is unverified.

### How it works today
- `papyrus login <site>` reads `https://<site>/.well-known/papyrus-cli.json`, runs Cognito hosted-UI Google sign-in with authorization code + PKCE on the site's public web client, loopback callback on localhost:3001. The session goes in the OS keychain via the shared cli-login library; no plaintext fallback.
- `papyrus login --remote <site>` prints an approval URL and code. The user approves on a phone with Google, and the CLI polls and receives the session. One broker per site in the site's own backend (Lambda function URL, DynamoDB TTL table, approval-pages Lambda). Off until `cliRemoteLogin` is set and `/cli/callback` is registered on the Cognito client.
- Prospectus is optional: enrollment is off unless `PAPYRUS_ENABLE_CLI_ENROLLMENT=true`; `cliOnFederationClient` (default off) is what points the CLI at the Prospectus client. Caveat: site-backend.ts still always creates the unused `prospectus-google-only` client.

### Options
| Option | Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A. Loopback PKCE on the web client (works now) | Nothing extra to deploy; Google only | Needs a browser and free port 3001 on the editor's machine; no cloud agents |
| B. A plus the per-site remote broker, enrollment and federation client off (recommended) | Phone approval and headless/cloud agents; broker holds no tokens; already built | A few Lambdas and a table; needs callback registration and a deploy (each needs Ryan's go-ahead); unused Prospectus client still created |
| C. Device-code flow | Familiar | Cognito has no RFC 8628; would need a custom broker, which is B |
| D. Paste or scrape a browser session token | Simple | Ruled out in PPY-5a3624 (no copy/paste of credentials); weaker secret handling |

### Papyrus changes
Functionally none to start. One optional change: let a deployment skip the Prospectus client. Draft, NOT filed:

Title: A Papyrus deployment can run with no Prospectus client or registration.
Description: Humorus runs one Papyrus deployment without Prospectus. site-backend.ts always adds `prospectus-google-only`. Add a flag (default: current behaviour) that skips the client and its outputs, and document the supported no-Prospectus CLI sign-in (local login plus `--remote`, enrollment and federation client off) in docs/cli-login.md.

```gherkin
Feature: A deployment signs in without Prospectus

  Scenario: No Prospectus client is created
    Given a site backend configured with the no-Prospectus flag
    When the backend is synthesized
    Then no prospectus-google-only client or its outputs exist
    And the web client still allows Google sign-in only

  Scenario: An editor signs in on a no-Prospectus site
    Given a site with cliRemoteLogin on and enrollment and federation client off
    When an editor runs papyrus login --remote
    Then the session is stored with no Prospectus call and no password user is created

  Scenario: Existing sites are unchanged
    Given the flag is absent
    Then the synthesized backend is identical to today's
```

### Open questions for Ryan
- Confirm the web client has no password flow (not verified; check amplify/auth/resource.ts before enabling).
- Skip the unused Prospectus client for Humorus (needs the Papyrus change), or tolerate it?
- Do editors work at desks with a browser (A), or is remote login the main path?
- Registering `https://<site>/cli/callback` and deploying the broker need approval once the account is ready.
